content: 1. Teach mothers how to heat-treat expressed breast milk to ensure it is safe for feeding. 2. Provide guidance to mothers on the appropriate quantity of expressed breast milk to feed their baby using a cup. 3. Educate mothers on recognizing signs that indicate their baby is receiving an adequate amount of milk, such as regular weight gain and sufficient wet diapers. 4. Weigh the baby regularly during the first month of life to monitor growth and assess weight gain. 5. Ensure proper maintenance of weighing scales to guarantee accurate measurements. 6. Offer specialized breastfeeding support to mothers who are not yet breastfeeding or are experiencing challenges. 7. Provide advice to mothers who are not breastfeeding on how to relieve breast engorgement effectively. 8. If the baby does not have a mother, ensure alternative feeding and care arrangements are in place. 9. Emphasize the importance of keeping the baby warm, especially for small or premature infants, through methods such as skin-to-skin contact. 10. Rewarm a baby who is cold using skin-to-skin techniques and ensure the baby’s environment is adequately warm. 11. Teach proper umbilical cord care to prevent infections. 12. Provide guidance on safe sleeping practices and maintaining hygiene for newborns. 13. In cases of newborn resuscitation, ensure the baby is kept warm, open the airway, and provide ventilation if the baby is not breathing. 14. If the baby is breathing less than 30 breaths per minute or shows severe chest in-drawing, stop ventilation and reassess. 15. If the baby is not breathing or gasping after 20 minutes of ventilation, follow appropriate protocols for cessation of resuscitation efforts. 16. Administer treatment and immunizations to the baby as needed, including intramuscular antibiotics during the first week of life. 17. If the mother tested RPR-positive, administer a single dose of intramuscular benzathine penicillin to the baby. 18. Provide intramuscular antibiotics for possible gonococcal eye infections in newborns. 19. Teach mothers how to administer treatments to their baby at home, including managing local infections. 20. Administer isoniazid (INH) prophylaxis to newborns at risk of tuberculosis. 21. Ensure newborns receive all recommended immunizations. 22. Provide antiretroviral (ARV) medications to newborns as indicated. 23. Advise mothers on when to return for routine and follow-up visits with their baby. 24. Encourage mothers to seek medical care promptly if their baby shows signs of illness or complications. 25. Refer babies urgently to a hospital if their condition requires advanced care. 26. Ensure the availability of essential equipment, supplies, drugs, and laboratory tests for pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum care. 27. Perform necessary laboratory tests, such as checking urine for protein, hemoglobin levels, and conducting rapid plasma reagin (RPR) tests for syphilis. 28. Interpret test results accurately to guide clinical decisions. 29. Conduct rapid HIV testing and provide appropriate counseling and care based on the results. 30. Offer comprehensive care during pregnancy, including preparing a birth and emergency plan. 31. Provide postpartum care for mothers and newborns, including breastfeeding support and care after an abortion if applicable. 32. Promote clean home delivery practices and educate families on maintaining hygiene during childbirth. 33. Maintain accurate records and forms, including referral records, feedback records, labor records, and postpartum records. 34. Use flowcharts and clinical decision-making tools to guide the management of routine and emergency care for women and newborns. 35. Emphasize the importance of early detection and management of complications during pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period. 36. Provide preventive measures, advice, and counseling to women and families to promote maternal and newborn health. 37. Adapt clinical guidelines to local needs and resources, ensuring they address endemic conditions and align with national treatment policies. 38. Train healthcare providers to use the guidelines effectively and provide high-quality care. 39. Promote the use of evidence-based interventions to reduce maternal and perinatal mortality and morbidity. 40. Ensure that healthcare facilities are equipped with essential drugs, supplies, and equipment to manage pregnancy, childbirth, and newborn care. 41. Provide counseling and key messages to women and families on topics such as breastfeeding, newborn care, and postpartum health. 42. Support women with special needs, including those living with HIV, and link them to community resources. 43. Follow universal precautions to prevent infections and ensure safe care practices. 44. Use color-coded flowcharts to classify conditions by severity and guide appropriate treatment and referral. 45. Provide detailed treatment and information pages linked to flowcharts for comprehensive care. 46. Offer simplified information sheets for mothers and families, adapted to local languages and conditions, to enhance understanding and compliance. 47. Promote hand hygiene and other preventive measures to reduce the risk of infections in healthcare and home settings. 48. Ensure timely and appropriate interventions for complications such as postpartum hemorrhage, pre-eclampsia, and eclampsia. 49. Provide vitamin A supplementation to mothers in the postpartum period as recommended. 50. Follow WHO guidelines for the prevention and management of maternal and perinatal infections.
